From 0f0c6415af409d213e7a132390a850c1251b92ef Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001 From: Akira Ajisaka Date: Tue, 10 May 2016 10:02:46 -0700 Subject: [PATCH] HADOOP-13118. Fix IOUtils#cleanup and IOUtils#closeStream javadoc. Contributed by Wei-Chiu Chuang. diff --git a/hadoop-common-project/hadoop-common/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/io/IOUtils.java b/hadoop-common-project/hadoop-common/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/io/IOUtils.java index 2588bf1f465..e6749b76bfa 100644 --- a/hadoop-common-project/hadoop-common/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/io/IOUtils.java +++ b/hadoop-common-project/hadoop-common/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/io/IOUtils.java @@ -234,7 +234,7 @@ public static void skipFully(InputStream in, long len) throws IOException { } /** - * Close the Closeable objects and ignore any {@link IOException} or + * Close the Closeable objects and ignore any {@link Throwable} or * null pointers. Must only be used for cleanup in exception handlers. * * @param log the log to record problems to at debug level. Can be null. @@ -255,7 +255,7 @@ public static void cleanup(Log log, java.io.Closeable... closeables) { } /** - * Closes the stream ignoring {@link IOException}. + * Closes the stream ignoring {@link Throwable}. * Must only be called in cleaning up from exception handlers. * * @param stream the Stream to close -- 2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **IOUtils.java**:
   - The Javadoc comment for the `cleanup` method was modified to indicate that it ignores any `Throwable`, instead of just `IOException`. 
   - Similarly, the Javadoc for the `closeStream` method was updated to specify that it ignores `Throwable` instead of only `IOException`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The changes in the Javadoc for both the `cleanup` and `closeStream` methods are related as they both clarify the methods' behavior regarding exception handling. By changing the reference from `IOException` to `Throwable`, the documentation now reflects a broader scope of exceptions that are ignored, enhancing the understanding of the methods' intended usage in cleanup scenarios. This consistency in documentation helps users of the `IOUtils` class recognize that both methods are designed to suppress all types of errors that may arise during resource cleanup.
